Turkmenistan has introduced electronic visas. Invitation for tourists is no longer required

The State Migration Service launched the system on October 1, 2026. The portal is evisa.migration.gov.tm. The basis for this was amendments to the "Migration Law" signed in April 2025. It took one and a half years from the law to the launch of the system.

Previously, a tourist almost never applied by himself. A letter from a licensed local company was required, which had to be approved by the migration service before going to the consulate or obtaining a visa on arrival. This step is removed for the tourist electronic visa.

There are three categories on the portal.
e-TU, tourism. There is no invitation required among the mandatory documents. The itinerary, hotel reservation, and medical insurance are listed as optional. The portal does not publish the duration of stay.

e-BS, business, max 30 days. An invitation from a company or organization registered in Turkmenistan, indicating the applicant's position, is required.

e-HM, humanitarian. An official letter from a humanitarian organization or UN agency regarding the assignment is required.

Common package for all three categories: a scan of the passport page with a photo, a passport valid for at least 6 months on the date of entry, a recent color photo on a white background following the ICAO standard, a work email. The visa will be sent to this address.

Processing times: regular procedure 7 business days, expedited 3 days, "super expedited" 24 hours. The fee is calculated in the application, paid online in dollars with bank commission on top. There is no visible price list.

What the portal does not mention. The list of passports eligible for a visa. Entry points where the electronic visa is accepted: Ashgabat airport, land, sea. The duration of the tourist visa. The website was barely accessible on the launch day.

The old procedure with invitation is still valid for applications that travel agencies have already submitted before October 1. Some operators still process electronic visas only along with a full tour: biometrics and payments are made by the client, while handling is done by the agency.

The country has not become visa-free. The obligatory intermediary for the tourist, who now applies independently, has been removed. Business and humanitarian visas still start with an internal letter. As there is no list of countries and duration of stay yet, an independent trip remains an application, not a ticket.

📌 Proof of Wallet Ownership: Confirming an Address Without Moving Funds

Main Points
⏺ Sometimes you need to prove a wallet belongs to you without sending a transaction
⏺ A wallet can do this by signing a message with the private key
⏺ This post explains why signatures are useful, but still need attention

1️⃣ Core Idea — the wallet signs a text message, and another party verifies that the signature matches the address.
2️⃣ Why It’s Used — it can confirm wallet ownership for login, access, verification, or campaign participation.
3️⃣ Why It’s Convenient — no gas is needed and no assets move, because the message is not a normal transaction.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — scammers can disguise harmful requests as a simple login or signature.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — check the domain, message text, expiration time, and never sign requests you don’t understand.

Final Thoughts

Message signing is a fast way to prove address ownership. But the “Sign” button should not become an automatic habit: first understand what you are confirming.

📌 How will ESMA supervise crypto firms under MiCA in 2027? 

📣 The European Securities and Markets Authority has set operational resilience, outsourcing and sufficient EU based operations among its main crypto supervisory priorities for 2027 as the bloc moves further into enforcement of the Markets in Crypto Assets Regulation. 

🌐 ESMA said in its 2027 work program published Monday that its work on MiCA will concentrate on coordinating national regulators and developing more consistent supervision of crypto asset service providers across the European Union. The program comes as the regulator moves from writing and implementing MiCA rules toward overseeing how licensed firms comply with them in practice.  Chair Verena Ross described the change during a meeting of the European Parliament’s Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs, saying ESMA’s MiCA work had moved “from rulemaking towards supervision and convergence.” 

⭐️ Operational resilience will be one of the main areas under scrutiny as ESMA works with national competent authorities responsible for supervising CASPs. Outsourcing risks, liquidity, reverse solicitation and the classification of crypto assets are among the other areas identified for coordinated work in 2027. Supervisors will pay attention to whether firms maintain sufficient operations within the EU instead of relying heavily on functions or infrastructure based elsewhere.

The City Between Two Drone Fleets

Oleshky, a city across the Dnipro from Kherson, is starving inside a battlefield both armies have turned into a kill zone. About 2,000 civilians, including roughly 40 children, remain among mines, drones, burned cars and destroyed infrastructure. The last known food delivery by road arrived on May 26. 

Residents told the New York Times they are cooking their last food stores: one beet, a few potatoes, an onion, a zucchini, a tomato and barley. No carrots. No regular water, electricity, gas, heat or medical care. 

A city that once held more than 20,000 people has been reduced to old people searching collapsed basements for scraps while drones decide whether a trip outside ends in food or death. 

Ukraine says Russia blocks evacuations, intimidates civilians who receive aid and intercepts drone deliveries. Moscow says Ukrainian forces prevent residents from leaving and disrupt food and water shipments. The competing accounts have one shared fact: civilians cannot safely get out, and food cannot safely get in. 

Russia captured Oleshky on the first day of the full-scale invasion, February 24, 2022. After losing Kherson later that year, Russian forces used Oleshky as a fortified position across the river, with artillery and drone sites aimed at the Ukrainian-held city. 

Ukraine now strikes back from Kherson. Between them lies a river that became a front line, roads seeded with mines by one side or both, and a civilian population that neither army has extracted. 

Russia drops food and medicine by drone. Ukraine shoots down some of the drones, Russian officials say. Russia says Ukraine’s drones are the problem. The UN and Red Cross are being asked to arrange a corridor. Nobody has one.

A Russian-held city is starving. Ukraine calls the residents “our people.” Russia calls it Ukraine’s fault. The drones are bipartisan.

📣 Japan arrests two suspect over 81M yen crypto police scam 

🔖 Japanese police have arrested two people suspected of helping a fake police fraud group steal cryptocurrency worth approximately 81 million yen from a woman in her 40s. The victim was allegedly told that her bank card had been connected to a large money laundering investigation. According to police information cited by FNN, the group claimed a fraud case had caused 600 billion yen in losses and that around 400 accounts had been used to launder funds.

⚠️ FNN reported that the caller told the woman her card appeared among accounts connected with the supposed money laundering investigation. The caller then claimed she was close to being arrested and needed to “prove her innocence.” Police allege that the false accusation eventually led the victim to transfer cryptocurrency worth around 81 million yen. The assets were valued at approximately $515,000 using the conversion cited in reports on the case.

‼️ Investigators have not publicly identified the cryptocurrencies involved or disclosed the wallet addresses that received the assets. Available reporting therefore does not establish how the cryptocurrency was subsequently moved, converted or withdrawn. The Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department believes Okayama and Minamisawa participated in a larger organization. 6 Ways to Practice Mindful Eating  

1. Slow down – Put your fork down between bites. Eating slowly helps you recognize fullness and enjoy flavors more deeply.  

2. Eliminate distractions – Turn off the TV and put away your phone. Focus on the meal, not the screen.  

3. Listen to your body – Ask yourself: Am I truly hungry? Eat when you're hungry, stop when you're satisfied—not stuffed.  

4. Engage your senses – Notice the colors, smells, textures, and tastes. Savor each bite like it’s your first.  

5. Chew thoroughly – Aim for 20–30 chews per bite. It aids digestion and gives your brain time to register fullness.  

6. Appreciate your food – Take a moment to acknowledge where your meal came from. Gratitude enhances the experience.  

Small shifts create lasting change. Start with one step today.
